b: Somewhere on your shopping list is a bass angler with more soft plastics than there are ornaments on the White House Christmas tree, yet they’ll still swear the one bait they’re missing is the one the fish want.
Buying for a bass angler has its pitfalls. Pick wrong and your gift lands in the corner of the garage next to three just like it. Pick right and it’s on the boat by spring.

Here’s the comforting part. According to the Recreational Boating & Fishing Foundation, 57 million Americans went fishing in 2025, nearly 43 million of them in freshwater. Federal surveys have long ranked black bass the most sought-after freshwater fish, with roughly four in ten freshwater anglers chasing them. That’s well north of 15 million bass anglers, and plenty of gear built with them in mind.
Translation? It’s virtually impossible to go wrong. Still, we did the legwork. Every pick comes from a brand we trust.
One more tip from the North Pole: shop around, because boy, are the deals out there this season!
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 25

Dice baits are having a moment, especially with smallmouth anglers, and the GBO rolls a winner. Ten hand-threaded silicone strands flow off a pyramid-shaped body scented with real bait. Go non-salted on a dropshot, free rig or wacky jig, or grab the salted version to fish weightless, since it’s denser, casts farther and sinks faster. A 4-pack has a retail price of $13.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 26

This wakebait has an old soul, developed with Nishine Lure Works and dressed in vintage looks. The 2.5-inch Mr. Fortune sports a hunched back, big forward-facing eyes and wing-like bill extensions that bounce it off wood, rock and weeds instead of hanging up. A mid-body blade gets it wobbling the instant the handle turns. Crawl it over shallow cover when bass are looking up. Retail price is $15.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 27

When the wind kicks up a chop, plenty of topwaters go quiet. The Wake Magic doesn’t. Its near 90-degree bill rolls the 4-inch, 1/2-ounce body across the surface, a steel-ball rattle rings the dinner bell and a prop-style tail blade throws flash and bubbles. Magnet weight transfer helps it sail on the cast. Developed with Lake Biwa guide Shinji Sato, it has a retail price of $24.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 28

Few baits have changed bass fishing like the bladed jig, and Z-Man owns the name. The ChatterBait Elite EVO starts humming the moment it hits the water, thanks to a patented direct head-to-blade connection and hex-shaped stainless blade. Upgrades include a heavy-duty 5/0 needlepoint hook, split-grip and wire trailer keepers and a wire-tied silicone skirt. Rip it through grass in 3/8 or 1/2 ounce. Retail price is $9.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 29

Small bait, big bites. The 1.5-inch Flutter Gizmo is a dice-style bait with hollow silicone legs that flutter at the slightest twitch, plus a wing-like tail that sends out subtle vibration as it slowly sinks. It mimics grass shrimp, bugs and baby crawfish, the kind of snack pressured bass rarely pass up. Power-shot or drop-shot it into tight cover on a size 2 wide gap hook. Retail price is $18.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 30
X Zone Lures Tungsten Tear Drop Drop Shot Weight

Drop shotting is a feel game, and tungsten wins it. These tear drops are 97% tungsten, so they’re smaller than lead and telegraph every pebble, sand patch and rock-pile edge straight to the rod hand. The teardrop shape slides through rocks instead of wedging in them, too. Pick pinch or tie-on styles from 1/8 to 3/4 ounce in green pumpkin. Retail price is $12.99 a pack.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 31
Do-It Molds Weedless Arky Kit w/Melter & Lead + Victory Hooks 10798 Jig Hooks

Every bass angler has a jig habit, and this pairing lets them feed it at home. The Arky is about as all-purpose as bass jigs get, made for skipping docks, dragging rock and pitching brush, and the kit bundles the weedless 1/4-, 3/8- and 1/2-ounce mold with a melter and lead. Fill it with Victory Hooks’ 10798, a black nickel, flat-eye jig hook with a sticky-sharp Endura Needle Point. The kit has a retail price of around $150, and the hooks are roughly $18 to $22 per hundred.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 32
Pro-Cure Super Gel Bass Pro Pack

The idea is simple. A bass that bites something tasting like real food hangs on longer. Pro-Cure Super Gel is made from real ground-up bait boosted with amino acids, and the Bass Pro Pack bundles three 2-ounce bottles: Trophy Bass, Crawfish and Garlic Crawfish. The sticky gel clings to soft plastics, jigs and swimbaits long after the splash. Retail price is $25.59.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 33

Clear line works in clear water. Bass don’t always live there. J-FLUORO Samurai Hidden Concept blends green and brown tints, so it disappears against grass, muddy bottoms and stained water. Underneath, it’s the same Made in Japan Samurai fluorocarbon anglers already trust, with a thin diameter, low stretch, minimal memory and long casts. Retail price starts at $29.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 34

Most braid floats, which isn’t ideal when the bass are down below. XBraid Sinking SS112 weaves four strands of braid with four strands of Ester line, so it slowly sinks for dropshots, mid-column presentations and forward-facing sonar work. High-vis yellow shows every tick and jump as the bait falls. It comes in 8 to 30 pound test, with retail prices starting at $25.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 35
EGO Fishing S2 Slider Landing Net

A good bass deserves a soft landing. Rubber mesh is easy on slime, scales and fins, and hooks don’t bury themselves in it the way they do in nylon. The S2 Slider’s telescoping handle slides out for reach and tucks back in for storage. For bass, the Medium or Large rubber nets fit the bill, with retail prices starting at $129.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 36

Every angler loses pliers. It’s practically a law of nature. The 2026 Slim Pliers are stainless steel with a titanium anti-corrosion coating, an outset tungsten carbide cutter that slices braid and fluorocarbon cleanly, and textured grips. A locking latch keeps them from snagging in a pocket or tackle bag. Choose 6.3 or 7.6 inches. Retail price is $39.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 37

Bank anglers, kayakers, or anyone jumping their buddy’s boat, this one’s for you. The EGO Tackle Box Backpack carries four clear 3600-series trays, with extra pockets for the odds and ends, laser-cut MOLLE loops for pliers and tools, and contoured straps for the long walk to the honey hole. It’s built from 1000D nylon with water-resistant PVC backing and wears Kryptek Pontus camo. Retail price is $159.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 38

Here’s one for the wall instead of the boat. These handcrafted wooden maps recreate a lake’s actual depths in layered 3D, so every point, flat and channel the angler loves hangs over the fireplace. More than 4,000 lakes are available. Retail prices run $129 to $579 depending on size, and each one is made to order.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 39

Bass anglers spend long days under a hard sun, and the Beacon Technical Hoodie has their backs. It’s UPF 50+ with a built-in neck gaiter and facemask, laser-cut vents and 4-way stretch. A water-repellant finish shrugs off light spray, while the fleece interior takes the bite out of cool spring mornings. A rear hood pass-through keeps the hood in place on a run across the lake. Retail price is $79.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 40

Hands take a beating on a bass boat, between sun, line and the occasional lip-grab. The Fish Monkey Pro365 Guide Glove brings UPF 50 protection, a non-slip silicone palm and a synthetic leather pad on the index finger to stop line cuts on long days of casting. Exposed fingers leave plenty of feel for tying knots and detecting bites. It’s breathable and quick-drying, too. Retail price is $32.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 41

Here’s the front door to the TATULA family. The Tatula X TW 100 brings Daiwa’s T-Wing System for smoother casts and MAGFORCE Z cast control, so backlashes stop being a holiday tradition. A Hyper Drive Design, UTD drag and swept handle round it out. It’s a dependable baitcaster for jigs, Texas rigs and crankbaits, with a retail price of $149.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 42

The judges at ICAST 2026 named it Best New Freshwater Rod, and it’s easy to see why. The Tatula Cork lineup offers 23 technique-specific bass rods, including two Glatech fiberglass models. High-density SVF graphite keeps them light and sensitive, X45 bias construction fights twist for accurate casts and solid hooksets, and premium cork grips finish the look. Every model has a retail price of $179.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 43
The Rod Glove Tournament Series (Spinning and Baitcasting)

Open a rod locker after a bumpy boat ride and you’ll find a tangle worthy of last year’s Christmas lights. The Rod Glove fixes that. Tournament Series sleeves are 2mm neoprene with reinforced openings and tips, plus a paracord tip loop and retaining cord. Spinning gloves fit rods 6’8″ to 7’6″ for a retail price of $10.99, and casting gloves fit 6’6″ to 7’6″ for $9.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 44

If one piece of gear determines success or failure, it’s the trolling motor, and the Ultrex QUEST is Minn Kota’s best. The brushless motor runs quiet and long, while Spot-Lock GPS anchoring holds the boat on a brushpile so the angler can keep casting instead of fiddling with the pedal. Retail price starts at $4,099.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 45

Not every bass angler needs GPS and a price tag to match. The Minn Kota Edge keeps it simple, pairing a cable-steer, heel-toe foot pedal with five speed settings and the same lifetime-guaranteed composite shaft found on the pricier models. Thrust runs from 45 pounds on 12 volts up to 70 pounds on 24, and the factory listed retail price is $549.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 46
Minn Kota X Series 7 CMSI+ Fish Finder

Humminbird’s sonar now lives under the Minn Kota name, and the new X7 CMSI+ is the friendliest way in. A bright 7-inch touchscreen shows crisp side and down imaging, maps come loaded, and the transducer is in the box, so it’s ready to rig. Pair it with an Ultrex QUEST and the angler can steer and anchor right from the screen. The 7-inch model has a retail price of $1,199.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 47
Norsk Lithium 36V + 28V 60AH Dual Voltage LiFePO4 Lithium Battery

Norsk’s Dual Voltage battery has two sets of terminals, 36 volts to run a trolling motor like the Ultrex QUEST and 28 volts to power forward-facing sonar so it runs cooler and longer. That’s one battery doing two jobs in a standard Group 31 footprint. Bluetooth monitoring, IP67 waterproofing and a 10-year warranty (12 with registration) seal the deal. Retail price is $1,199.99.
2026 Bass Fishing Gift Guide: Gear Picks From Rod Deck to Tackle Bag 48

Lithium or lead-acid, trolling motor batteries only perform when they’re properly charged, and Battery Tender has a marine lineup to handle it. Onboard WaveCharge models top off multiple banks at once, PowerPlus chargers cover 24-, 36- and 48-volt systems, and simple 12-volt maintainers keep a battery healthy through the off-season. Retail prices start at $64.95.
